title: Etale restriction commutes with canonical compact-support composition
statement:
Let $A,B$ be finite commutative rings and $\varphi:A\to B$ a unital homomorphism. Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be quasi-compact morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], with fixed compactifications of $f,g,fg$. Write $F_{h,R}=Rh_{!,R}$ on $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support], $U_T=D^+(\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi,T})$, and $c_h:F_{h,A}U_{\mathrm{source}(h)}\xrightarrow{\sim}U_{\mathrm{target}(h)}F_{h,B}$ for the proper/open restriction comparison, whose open factor is the inverse unit mate and whose proper factor is the derived direct-image restriction comparison [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change]. Let $\alpha_R:F_{g,R}F_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{fg,R}$ be the canonical chosen-compactification compositor [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons]. Then for every $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$,
$$\alpha_{A,U_XL}\,;\,c_{fg,L}=F_{g,A}(c_{f,L})\,;\,c_{g,F_{f,B}L}\,;\,U_Z(\alpha_{B,L}),$$
where semicolons mean composition in order from left to right. Both sides have source $F_{g,A}F_{f,A}U_XL$ and target $U_ZF_{fg,B}L$. No scalar extension or tensor presentation is involved.

proof.text: Use the canonical compactification triangle Compactification.Triangle.ofHasCompactification of f,g, obtained from the supplied compactifications of g and fg by Compactification.ofComp and restriction. This construction needs no qcqs hypothesis or new application of Nagata. The canonical compositor comparison theorem computes its component as proper composition, open composition and cartesian proper/open interchange, conjugated by the chosen-compactification comparisons.

proof.text: Commute scalar restriction through proper composition using the resolution-normalized direct-image comparison. For open composition, take the open-adjunction transpose; both paths identify the same inverse image and the same unit. For mixed interchange, paste the scalar inverse-image square with its cartesian inverse-image square and take mates. These three equations give the restriction square for the compatible triangle.

proof.text: For the chosen compactifications use the canonical refinement factors. Each is proper pushforward of the proper/open comparison, so the same mate square commutes with it. Cancel the inverse refinement factors. This gives the displayed equation with exactly the specified compositor and restriction comparisons.

theorem compactSupportRestrictionPlus_compositor
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiCompact g]
    [HasCompactification f] [HasCompactification g] [HasCompactification (f ≫ g)]
    (L : DerivedCategory.Plus (Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B))) :
    (rightDerivedLowerShriekPlusCompIso A f g).hom.app
        ((Sheaf.restrictScalars X.smallEtaleTopology φ).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.obj L) ≫
      (compactSupportCoefficientRestrictionPlus φ
        (HasCompactification.compactification (f ≫ g))).hom.app L =
    (rightDerivedLowerShriekPlus (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) g).map
        ((compactSupportCoefficientRestrictionPlus φ
          (HasCompactification.compactification f)).hom.app L) ≫
      (compactSupportCoefficientRestrictionPlus φ
        (HasCompactification.compactification g)).hom.app
          ((rightDerivedLowerShriekPlus (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) f).obj L) ≫
      (Sheaf.restrictScalars Z.smallEtaleTopology φ).mapDerivedCategoryPlus.map
        ((rightDerivedLowerShriekPlusCompIso B f g).hom.app L)
